newsitem.title: RUSSIA: BASKETBALL-UNPAID DYNAMO MOSCOW DROP STRIKE THREAT.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-UNPAID DYNAMO MOSCOW DROP STRIKE THREAT.

text.p: The unhappy basketball players of Dynamo Moscow, who have not been paid since the summer, backed down on Wednesday from a threat to strike and agreed to play Thursday's Euroleague match against Spain's Caja San Fernando.

"The team decided we'll turn out tomorrow and in the last match of our Euroleague group and will, naturally, play to win each game. There's no point adding anything," Dynamo player Oleg Meleshchenko told Russia's NTV television.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted a Russian Basketball Federation official saying the players had been told a schedule for paying them the money owed to them would be worked out in a week.
Federation president Sergei Belov urged the long-suffering players to abandon their planned strike in the name of patriotism, NTV said.
It said the players, unpaid since July, had been told on Tuesday their wages were being almost halved and they would have to pay their own taxes out of what was left.
Some are considering transfers to more prosperous clubs.

The Dynamo players are by no means the only Russians to suffer. Millions of other people are in the same position as a web of company debts, unpaid wages and tax arrears ensnares the creaking economy.
